module.title: CSS basics
module.description: Colors, sizes and fonts: give your page some style.

ex0.title: Paint it purple
ex0.guide: HTML gives a page its content, CSS gives it its looks! Here the HTML is ready: we only change the style.
mission: A CSS rule picks elements with a selector (h1) and changes their look with declarations (color: purple;).
In style.css, make the title purple, then make the paragraph text 20px big.
dialogue0: Hello, we are your new clients. We would like to have a nice website. We are not sure what we want yet, though.
dialogue1: I know! I want a big header where my name is written! 'Haku' in very big, it sounds nice.
hint0: Do you need help? I'm here for you!
ex0.lesson:
A CSS rule has two parts:

  • the selector (h1, p...) says which elements are styled;
  • the declarations between { } say how: property: value;

The HTML loads the CSS file with this line in its <head>:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">

ex1.title: Link your style
ex1.guide: This time the CSS is ready, but the page doesn't use it yet. Let's connect them!
mission:
1. In index.html, load the stylesheet: add this line inside <head>.
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">

2. The CSS styles elements with the class story: give the <div> this attribute.
class="story"
3. In style.css, give the title the color you like.
hint0: The <head> can't be edited in blocks mode: switch to Code for step 1.
hint1: In blocks mode, hover the <div> and click + to add an attribute: name class, value story.
hint2: Click a selector chip in the CSS blocks (like h1) to create a rule, then add a color property to it.
ex1.lesson:
HTML and CSS are two files that work together:

  • <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> tells the browser to load the CSS;
  • a class (class="story") names elements, and the selector .story styles them all.
